business_scope.primary_industry_name: Blank-Check Entity for Public Market Acquisition Mergers (SPAC)

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (private and commercial matters in Quebec are governed by the Civil Code of Quebec, while federal AML/CFT, criminal and securities frameworks apply; the target vehicle is a Quebec civil-law limited partnership, société en commandite, with a federal and provincial regulatory overlay)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA)
Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP)
Canada-China Foreign Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (FIPA, in force 2014)
Canada-United States Tax Convention (1980, as amended)
Canada-United Kingdom and Northern Ireland Tax Treaty (1966, as amended)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c. 17 (PCMLTFA) and Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations, SOR/2002-184 (PEP and beneficial ownership rules); Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c. C-46, s. 83.05 (terrorist entity listing) and s. 462.31 (money laundering offences); Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c. 17 and United Nations Act, SC 1992, c. 17 (sanctions and asset freezing); Quebec Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1 (ARE), including the beneficial ownership disclosure regime applicable to sociétés en commandite; Quebec Securities Act, CQLR c. V-1.1, together with AMF instruments governing prospectus filing, continuous disclosure and blank-check/SPAC transactions.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Existence / Good Standing issued by the home jurisdiction corporate registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry or companies registrar in the country of origin of each foreign partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization where the country of origin is not party to the Hague Apostille Convention)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency identifying the general partner, all limited partners and their registered addresses
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registered agent, corporate secretary or notary-public of the home entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization followed by Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization and, where required, sworn French translation by a certified Quebec translator

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Beneficial ownership declaration and organizational chart for every natural person holding 25% or more of the partnership interests or control
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed AML/CFT counsel or notary-public of the home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized declaration with Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization for use before the Registraire des entreprises du Québec and FINTRAC

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of the partnership deed / limited partnership agreement (constituent instrument)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization; sworn French translation to be attached to the REQ declaration

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney authorizing the Quebec-based person to execute the REQ registration declaration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: General partner or authorized agent of the home entity, executed before a notary in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization of the original, followed by notarization of the French-language version by a Quebec notary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized passport, proof of residential address and bank reference letters for each general partner and beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority, utility provider, financial institution and certifying notary of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified copies by the notary of origin; bank reference letters transmitted directly to AML/CFT counsel as a risk-based control, with apostille only when expressly required by the receiving institution

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of the general partner, all limited partners holding 25% or more, directors, officers and authorized representatives against: Global Affairs Canada consolidated sanctions lists under the Special Economic Measures Act and the United Nations Act; the UN Security Council Consolidated List; the Criminal Code domestic terrorist entity list (s. 83.05); OFAC SDN List and the EU Consolidated List as cross-border best practice; and Quebec securities disqualification databases (AMF cease-trade orders, registration revocations and statutory disqualifications). PEP identification is mandatory under PCMLTFA s. 9.3 and applies to foreign PEPs, domestic PEPs, heads of international organizations, and their family members and close associates. Each PEP determination must be recorded in the onboarding file with enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds and source-of-wealth evidence, and senior compliance approval. All transactions are subject to FINTRAC large cash transaction reporting above CAD 10,000, suspicious transaction reporting as soon as practicable (immediately for terrorism-financing grounds), and record-keeping obligations for five years. For SPAC escrow and trust structures, additional verification of the trustee, custodians and each investor contributing to the investment trust is required.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ), Registre des entreprises — https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language, CQLR c. C-11, ss. 82-91, and the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1, ss. 13-20, the declared name of the enterprise must be in French and must include the legal form designation société en commandite (S.E.C.) or Limited Partnership (L.P.). A non-French version may be registered only where the enterprise's head office or principal establishment is outside Quebec or where the Registrar authorizes a non-French name. Latin-script transliteration is required; the name must be distinctive, not confusingly similar to an existing registration, and must comply with French orthographic and terminological norms.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Corporation / Inc. (inconsistent with the partnership legal form)
SPAC / Special Purpose Acquisition (requires prior AMF securities clearance for prospectus and listing use)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of a name reservation by the REQ, counsel for the applicant shall, within 30 calendar days of the notification, file a written reconsideration request with the Registrar under ARE s. 29, accompanied by any remedial evidence, including a consent letter from the holder of a conflicting name, proof of registration of a relevant trademark, and a French-language legal opinion. A revised name may be re-filed with a new application and the statutory fee (CAD 33), which restarts the 60-day reservation window and preserves priority where no conflicting reservation was lodged in the interim. If the Registrar confirms the refusal, judicial review may be sought before the Court of Québec under ARE s. 43 within 30 days of the final decision, with the court empowered to order issuance of the name certificate.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or serviced commercial address located in Quebec is generally accepted by the REQ for a société en commandite, provided the address is a genuine establishment address in Quebec, can receive service of process and maintains the statutory records. For SPAC-related listing and AMF policy expectations, however, the regulator will scrutinize substantive management presence: the vehicle should maintain a Quebec-based general partner representative, financial records, minutes of partnership meetings, and segregated escrow account documentation at the declared address. A pure mail-forwarding address is insufficient to establish commercial substance once a prospectus is filed or an exchange listing is sought.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low, approximately 7% annual probability for a Quebec limited partnership in normal course; the REQ primarily monitors address and partner information through correspondence, declarations and registry updates. Unannounced on-site inspection risk rises materially to approximately 20-30% where the SPAC files a prospectus with the AMF and enters the public market, because securities regulators and FINTRAC may pursue document-based examinations and trust-account verifications; FINTRAC examinations do not involve routine warrantless premises entry.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood_summary: Low baseline with material uplift upon SPAC public filing and enhanced AML/CFT review.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Québec, articles 2236-2246 (Limited Partnership); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c. P-44.1) for registration; Québec Securities Act (CQLR c. V-1.1) and National Instrument 41-101 for SPAC prospectus issuance
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) / Québec Enterprise Registrar
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration d'immatriculation - société en commandite (Registration Statement of a Limited Partnership)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under Québec law; limited partners must contribute tangible capital as stipulated in the partnership agreement (CCQ art. 2244). For SPAC operations, 100% of gross offering proceeds must be deposited into a qualified trust escrow account prior to unit issuance, in compliance with AMF securities directives and the partnership agreement.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) The subscription agreements and initial capital contributions of the limited partners are accepted, and the general partner is directed to deposit all offering proceeds into the designated qualified trust escrow account. (2) The registered office of the Partnership is established at 1250 René-Lévesque Blvd West, Montréal, Québec, and the registration statement shall be filed with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec. (3) John A. Smith is appointed as Chief Executive Officer and principal manager of the general partner, with exclusive authority to sign all regulatory filings, notarial declarations, banking resolutions, and licensing applications. (4) All prior inconsistent acts are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Search and Reservation with the Québec Enterprise Registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) – online name reservation service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS search comprising the proposed name with the legal suffix 'L.P.' or 'S.E.C.'; file a name reservation application indicating the intended Quebec head office; pay the prescribed fee; retain the attestation valid for 90 days during which the partnership agreement and registration statement must be completed.
required_dossiers: Completed name reservation application form for a limited partnership
Identification documents of the general partner and its authorized representative
Power of attorney or board resolution of the general partner if the application is filed by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the requested name is refused due to similarity or non-distinctiveness, file a new reservation with an amended distinctive element or request a formal review (demande de révision) of the REQ decision within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization of the Limited Partnership Agreement (Contrat de société en commandite)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Chambre des notaires du Québec (a notary practicing in Québec)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the limited partnership agreement under CCQ arts. 2236-2246, clearly identifying general and limited partners, capital contribution schedule, profit-sharing ratios, SPAC business purpose encompassing public market acquisitions and mergers, trust escrow mechanics, and dissolution terms; execute the agreement before a Québec notary with all partner signatures and notarial attestation.
required_dossiers: Draft limited partnership agreement
Name reservation attestation issued by REQ
Certified copy of the constitutive documents and registry extract of the corporate general partner
Certified passports or identity records of all partners with AML/KYC evidence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary raises validity or capacity concerns, execute a notarial rectification act (acte rectificatif) or restate the partnership agreement before the same or another notary at no additional registration penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of the Limited Partnership with the Enterprise Registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) – online filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Déclaration d'immatriculation electronically to REQ, containing the partnership name, Québec registered office address, municipality, legal form, full identification of the general partner and of each limited partner, and the object of the partnership; pay the statutory filing fee and obtain the registration certificate and Québec enterprise number (NEQ).
required_dossiers: Notarized limited partnership agreement
Name reservation attestation
Proof of the Québec registered office address (lease, title, or notarial attestation)
Identification and eligibility declarations of the general partner and limited partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: On a REQ query or refusal, file a supplementary declaration (déclaration complémentaire) curing the deficiencies within 60 days; if the registration is improperly processed, a declaration of rectification can be filed retroactively bearing no effect on partnership validity from execution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Securities Issuer and SPAC Prospectus Licensing with the AMF
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF) – Direction des prospectus
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a preliminary and final long-form prospectus for the initial public offering of SPAC units/Class A shares, including trust escrow arrangements, redemption rights, acquisition criteria, and sponsor compensation; request a receipt for the prospectus in Québec; satisfy NI 41-101, NI 81-102 (investment fund restrictions) and cross-border listing requirements where the units will also trade on a U.S. exchange via SEC registration; pay the AMF expected filing fees.
required_dossiers: Final prospectus prepared per Form 41-101F1
Qualified trust escrow agreement executed with the trustee
Audited balance sheet or exemptive relief documentation for the blank-check issuer
AML/ATF program and risk assessment compliant with FINTRAC and AMF Policy 11-202
Organizational governance materials: partnership agreement, general partner resolutions, and KYC records of all officers, directors and sponsors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to AMF deficiency letters and comment sheets by refiling amended prospectus pages; if a receipt is denied, request a hearing before the AMF Bureau de décision et de révision or seek exemptive relief under National Instrument 11-102 coordinating provincial and U.S. recognition.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Environmental and Occupational Clearance for Administrative-Office SPAC Status
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP) and the local fire safety service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm that the registered office operates solely as an administrative and financial head office with no physical manufacturing, combustive, or discharge activities; obtain MELCCFP confirmation of exemption from the mandatory EIA regime; secure the municipal occupancy permit and fire safety certificate; register the workplace with CNESST and obtain an occupational health attestation for personnel.
required_dossiers: MELCCFP exemption request for administrative non-discharge activity
Building occupancy permit issued by the municipality
Fire safety certificate from the local fire safety service
CNESST employer registration and prevention program statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MELCCFP classifies the SPAC as a non-exempt establishment, submit a written justification confirming zero emissions and zero effluent; any future de-SPAC target with industrial assets will require an independent full EIA prior to acquisition closing in accordance with the Environmental Quality Act (CQLR c. Q-2, art. 22).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration and Trust Escrow Account Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec, Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), and a Canadian Schedule I chartered bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the limited partnership for Québec sales tax (QST) and GST via Revenu Québec (form RP-5000) and obtain a CRA business number where required; open a dedicated trust escrow account with a Canadian Schedule I bank and execute the trust agreement stipulating that offering proceeds remain in escrow until the SPAC acquisition conditions are met; provide the bank with the REQ certificate and AML/KYC clearance.
required_dossiers: REQ registration certificate and NEQ number
Notarized limited partnership agreement
AML/KYC identification for all authorized signatories and beneficial partners
Completed RP-5000 GST/QST registration forms
Trust escrow agreement and trustee mandate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax or escrow activation is deficient, file an amending declaration with Revenu Québec and provide corrected trust instructions to the bank; any delay in escrow sign-off is cured by completing residence-address and beneficial-ownership attestations and executing an amended escrow instruction letter retroactively effective on first deposit.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF) for financial and securities licensing; MELCCFP for environmental status review of the administrative office
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Prospectus Receipt and Issuer Registration for a Blank-Check Acquisition Corporation (SPAC) under the Québec Securities Act; supplemented by an Environmental Exemption Attestation for non-discharge administrative use

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP), Québec
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category C – Exempt from mandatory EIA for administrative office use; any de-SPAC target ownership of industrial facilities will require a Category I full EIA report and ministerial authorization under the Environmental Quality Act (art. 22) before construction or operation
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater, VOC or combustion emissions are generated by the SPAC head office. Post-de-SPAC, acquired facilities must comply with the Québec Clean Air Regulation (CQLR c. Q-2, r. 4.1) limiting VOC to 250 mg/m³ in dry stack gases, and the Water Environment Protection Regulation (CQLR c. Q-2, r. 13) requiring, inter alia, COD ≤ 240 mg/L, TSS ≤ 45 mg/L and pH 6.0-9.5; residual hazardous waste must be managed per the Regulation respecting the recovery and reclamation of residual materials.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Mandatory civil defense clearance: (i) fire safety certificate issued by the competent municipal fire safety service pursuant to the Québec Building Act and Fire Safety Code; (ii) structural load and occupancy certification confirming A-2 office class; and (iii) CNESST workplace safety clearance and a written prevention program where staffing exceeds 20 employees after de-SPAC integration.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — My Business Account portal for federal GST/HST and corporate income tax; Revenu Québec — CliC SÉUR portal for Quebec provincial income tax, QST, and payroll obligations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident limited partnership entering Quebec must first obtain a federal Business Number (BN) from the CRA, either online or by completing Form RC348 (Request for a Business Number and GST/HST Account). Once the BN is issued, the partnership or its appointed representative must register for the GST/HST account. For Quebec provincial purposes, the same BN or a separate Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ) must be obtained from Revenu Québec; the partnership must file Form LE-12 or register through CliC SÉUR. Registration for QST is required if the partnership makes taxable supplies in Quebec exceeding the small-supplier threshold or if it is a non-resident operating a commercial enterprise in Quebec.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible; a Canadian limited partnership is fiscally transparent for income tax purposes, with income, gains, credits, and losses flowing through to partners; however, for GST/HST and QST the partnership itself is treated as a separate registrant for supplies made in its own right. No designated tax-exempt zone applies in Canada or Quebec.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not operate a check-the-box entity classification regime. A limited partnership is structurally characterized as a pass-through under subsection 96(1) of the Income Tax Act. Partnerships may make certain elections for computation and fiscal period purposes, including the election under subsection 249.1(4) to shorten a fiscal period, and may choose between the Accrual and Cash methods for GST/HST only if the small-supplier threshold is met. Hybrid mismatch rules under sections 12.6 and 18.4 of the Income Tax Act may disallow deductions for certain payments under hybrid arrangements, but no entity classification election is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST (Goods and Services Tax) at federal level; QST (Quebec Sales Tax) as a parallel provincial value-added tax administered by Revenu Québec; no harmonized sales tax in Quebec.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 per calendar year in worldwide taxable supplies for GST/HST small-supplier qualification; Quebec QST registration mirrors the CAD 30,000 threshold for taxable supplies having a place of supply in Quebec. Non-resident partnerships carrying on a business in Canada generally must register regardless of the threshold once they are not a small supplier.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada maintains no national real-time e-invoice clearance or fiscal stamping regime for GST/HST. Registrants must issue valid invoices containing prescribed information and retain all records in Canada or make them available electronically to CRA and Revenu Québec on demand. Electronic filing and remittance through CRA My Business Account and Revenu Québec CliC SÉUR is mandatory for registrants with annual revenues exceeding established thresholds. API-based EDI invoice exchange is permitted, but no government-operated pre-clearance or imprinting is required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A limited partnership may claim the 0% GST/HST and 0% QST rate for qualifying exports of tangible personal property delivered to non-residents and removed from Canada, and for certain supplies of services performed for non-residents if the services are not taxable in Canada. The export must be supported by commercial invoices, shipping records, and evidence of export; for offshore services, the contract must clearly indicate an offshore recipient and direct benefit outside Canada. For Quebec QST, the same zero-rating principles apply, but a separate certificate of export may be required.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (CBSA Form A1 / Canada Customs Invoice or electronic equivalent through the Canadian International Trade Single Window)
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill with proof of physical departure from Canada
Inward Remittance Certificate or equivalent bank wire confirmation evidencing the export sale proceeds from the foreign purchaser
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: False or exaggerated export zero-rating claims are subject to audit by both the CRA and Revenu Québec. A denied claim results in immediate reassessment, repayment of the unremitted GST/HST or QST, interest compounding daily, and civil penalties under subsection 285(1) of the Excise Tax Act for repeated omission or misstatement. Willful fraud or intentional misrepresentation attracts criminal prosecution, fines of up to PDQ 200,000 or an amount equal to the tax evaded, and imprisonment up to five years. For QST, parallel enforcement powers under the Taxation Act and the Act respecting the Quebec Sales Tax apply, including penalties of up to 200% of the amount evaded in aggravated cases.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); Canada has no single foreign-exchange administration—regulatory authority is shared among the Department of Finance Canada, FINTRAC (cross-border transaction reporting), OSFI (prudential supervision), Global Affairs Canada (economic sanctions), and the Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF) for Quebec securities and escrow matters.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada is an IMF Article VIII member: both current-account and capital-account transactions are fully convertible, and no exchange-control licence is required for investor subscriptions, IPO trust deposits, business-combination consideration, or profit/dividend remittances. Practical remittance hurdles: (i) FINTRAC reporting for every incoming/outgoing wire ≥ CAD 10,000; (ii) Part XIII non-resident withholding tax of 25% (treaty-reduced) on interest, dividends, and certain management fees; (iii) AMF/TSX escrow-release conditions attached to SPAC trust funds; (iv) Investment Canada Act net-benefit review if the de-SPAC target exceeds statutory monetary thresholds.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no export-proceeds surrender rule, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no statutory repatriation timeline for foreign-currency export receipts. Exporters may retain export proceeds in any currency, subject only to CBSA electronic export declarations for shipments exceeding CAD 2,000 and to Income Tax Act record-keeping requirements. The SPAC is not an exporter; its USD IPO/trust proceeds are freely holdable in Canadian, US, or offshore clearing accounts.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)
Laurentian Bank of Canada (Banque Laurentienne du Canada)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW as primary treasury or SPAC trust custodian; MEDIUM strictly as an ancillary payment-only corridor. Legal constraints: foreign digital EMIs (e.g., Wise, Payoneer, Airwallex) are classified as money services businesses (MSBs) under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act and must register with FINTRAC before serving Canadian clients; they lack CDIC deposit insurance; they cannot act as a qualified custodian or licensed trustee for SPAC escrow/trust proceeds under AMF and TSX rules; and they cannot clear Canadian-dollar high-value payments over Lynx. Therefore, all trust-era funds must sit with a Canadian-resident Schedule I bank or a federally/Quebec-licensed trust company.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Fully remote account opening is the exception, not the rule. For SPAC/LP structures, Canadian banks generally require at least one director or the General Partner's authorised officer to attend an in-person interview at a Canadian branch, or a live video interview with notarised identification and confirmation by a Canadian-licensed lawyer; the bank will not rely solely on self-attesting offshore directors. The Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) extract, certificated general partner resolution, UBO attestation, and source-of-funds/wealth statements must be delivered within 10 business days of onboarding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership concealment through the LP/GP layered structure common to blank-check IPO sponsors.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised UBO register with chain-of-title to each natural person holding 10% or more; REQ certificate of registration for the General Partner; certified copy of the limited partnership agreement and GP resolutions; source-of-wealth declarations; sponsor lock-up/escrow agreement; legal opinion confirming the absence of bearer shares or bearer partnership interests.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound wire subscriptions from private-placement investors domiciled in high-risk or sanctioned jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Per-investor KYC pack comprising passport, proof of address, accredited-investor/exempt-status certificate, signed subscription agreement, and source-of-funds statement; originator BIC and correspondent-bank details verified against the Canadian Sanctions List (Global Affairs SEMA) and OFAC; FINTRAC suspicious transaction report filed if any facts give rise to reasonable grounds for suspicion.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Activation of the SPAC trust/escrow account with IPO proceeds from underwriters without a clear third-party custodial mandate.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Final prospectus with AMF receipt and underwriting agreement; certified escrow/trust agreement designating the bank or a licensed trust company as trustee; written confirmation that no sponsor, director, or officer can withdraw trust assets before a qualified business combination; audit trail linking the underwriter's MT103 to the trust ledger.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large outbound payments to target shareholders in a foreign jurisdiction following a de-SPAC transaction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business-combination agreement and shareholder-approved plan of arrangement; AMF/TSX listing approval; alphabetical beneficiary payment schedule with completed sanctions screening; board resolution authorising each wire; pre-transaction notification to the bank's financial crimes unit for any payment exceeding CAD 1,000,000.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Private-placement subscriptions: SWIFT MT103 to the operational account with the purpose statement 'Subscription for limited partnership units – ISIC 6499 SPAC' plus the investor's unique subscription code. IPO gross proceeds: underwriter wires via MT103/MT202 COV directly to the trust/escrow account at the custodian trust company. Verification: FINTRAC large-transaction reporting for wires ≥ CAD 10,000, sanctions-list screening of originator and beneficiary, and reconciliation to the subscription register. Canada has no statutory wire purpose-code table; the bank's instruction form requires a semantic purpose statement. CAD/USD conversion of received funds is executed at the corporate dealing desk under a dated foreign-exchange contract; no Bank of Canada approval is required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Domestic CAD disbursements settle over Lynx (Canada's high-value payment system; formerly LVTS) or Interac for de minimis amounts. Cross-border USD settles via the bank's U.S. correspondent network (CHIPS/Fedwire) using SWIFT MT103 and MT202 COV cover payments. Trade-related settlements may be structured as documentary remittances, irrevocable commercial letters of credit governed by UCP600, or standby letters of credit governed by ISP98 issued by a Canadian Schedule I bank. Every outbound wire ≥ CAD 10,000 is reported to FINTRAC; all beneficiary parties are screened against Canadian SEMA sanctions, OFAC, and the Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CAD/USD FX forward (up to 18 months) under an ISDA/FXC master agreement
FX swap (spot-forward swap combination) for bridge financing windows
Cross-currency swap (CAD/USD) to hedge business-combination consideration
Plain-vanilla CAD/USD foreign-exchange options (purchaser side only, no naked option writing)
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) limited to illiquid or restricted target-country currencies; unnecessary for CAD/USD due to deep deliverable liquidity

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) to the Registraire des entreprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of the limited partnership's registration in the Quebec enterprise register; reminders are issued by REQ for the annual filing season
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of approximately CAD 200; administrative strike-off of the registration after registrar's notice and a 30-day lapse; reinstatement and regularizing fees apply, and contracts entered during the lapse may be unenforceable

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return (Canada Revenue Agency)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Five months after the partnership's fiscal period end; for a December 31 fiscal year end, the return is due May 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CAD 25 per day late-filing penalty up to CAD 2,500, plus failure-to-file penalties under the Income Tax Act; incorrect or unreported partner allocations attract CRA reassessment, interest, and gross negligence penalties

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: RL-15 Partnership Information Slips and annual information reporting to Revenu Québec
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: S slips must be filed with Revenu Québec and provided to partners by the last day of February following the calendar year (e.g., February 28, 2025 for the 2024 calendar year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty for failure to file an information slip or return: CAD 100 minimum up to CAD 3,600, plus interest; intentional omissions attract higher penalties under the Quebec Taxation Act

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual reporting issuer filings (annual financial statements, MD&A, Annual Information Form) through SEDAR+
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF) / Canadian Securities Administrators (CSA) via SEDAR+
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days of fiscal year-end for non-investment reporting issuers under National Instrument 51-102; interim filings within 45 days of each interim period end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filings trigger notice of default, cease trade orders, reporting issuer delinquency listings, late filing fees charged by securities regulators, and potential suspension or delisting of the SPAC securities

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Quebec limited partnership operating as a public SPAC listing vehicle is a reporting issuer; annual financial statements must be audited by an independent public accountant licensed in Canada and qualified under the Quebec Securities Act and National Instrument 51-102. Non-reporting limited partnerships are not statutorily required to file audited financial statements, but SPAC trust/escrow arrangements and offering or listing covenants normally mandate a certified annual audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) for reporting issuers and publicly accountable enterprises; Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) is available only for non-listed limited partnerships that are not publicly accountable.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Quebec enterprise registration law requires the limited partnership, through its general partner, to confirm ultimate beneficiary information annually as part of the REQ annual declaration. Any transfer of partnership interests that alters the ultimate beneficial ownership must be declared to REQ as a modification within 30 days of the transfer. The register of partners must be updated contemporaneously at each transfer and reconciled at year-end; failure to update or confirm exposes the partnership and the general partner to monetary penalties.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Partners (Registre des associés commandités et commanditaires)
Register of General Partner's Directors and Officers (for corporate general partner)
Minute Book of the General Partner and Partnership Resolutions
Ultimate Beneficiary Register (Registre des bénéficiaires ultimes)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600 – 1,500 per annum (Quebec registered office, process agent, and corporate secretarial support)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 45,000 – 100,000 per annum for a SPAC public issuer audit; USD 8,000 – 20,000 per annum for a non-reporting limited partnership without a public audit mandate

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined general corporate rate in Quebec (federal 15% + Quebec 11.5%); the limited partnership itself is fiscally transparent, so this rate applies to corporate partners on their allocated Canadian-source income, not to the LP entity.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday is available to a SPAC limited partnership. The LP is pass-through and ordinarily incurs no entity-level income tax. Corporate partners may claim the general federal and Quebec rates as above; the Canadian small business deduction is unavailable to broadly held or public-market-oriented investment vehicles. Deductions and credits of general application (e.g., scientific research and experimental development credits, Quebec investment tax credits) may be available only where the SPAC carries on real business activity. Absent genuine commercial activity, claims are contestable under the general anti-avoidance rule (GAAR).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T5013 — Partnership Information Return and T5013 slips; filed with the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) through CRA Internet File Transfer, My Business Account, or Represent a Client Portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; one return for each fiscal period of the limited partnership, accompanied by T5013 slips for each limited partner.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: No later than five months after the partnership's fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year partnership, the deadline is June 30 of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name of the limited partnership, CRA business number (BN), registered office address, fiscal period-end, and general partner contact information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the partnership's own BN; do not enter the BN or tax account number of a non-resident limited partner in the partnership header. Foreign partners must be identified only in the partner schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part I — Statement of Partnership Income / Schedule 1
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate gross revenue, deductions, and net income or loss by source; followed by an allocation schedule showing each partner's percentage share of each income class.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident limited partners, show only Canadian-source income and any income reasonably attributable to a Canadian permanent establishment or Canadian taxable property. Portfolio foreign income of the LP that is not taxable in Canada should be removed from the Canadian column.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Each partner's allocated share of the limited partnership's net business income or loss from active trading, acquisition, or escrow-management activities.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident limited partner carrying on business through the LP is liable to Part I tax on this amount unless a tax treaty assigns the taxing right only to the partner's residence. Attach the relevant treaty exemption reference to the partnership files.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocated taxable capital gains and allowable capital losses from dispositions of Canadian taxable property, including shares of private target corporations if applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the non-resident partner has no permanent establishment in Canada and the disposed property is not taxable Canadian property, treaty protection may exempt the gain; such relief must be documented with a valid Tax Residency Certificate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculation of each limited partner's at-risk amount; determines the amount of partnership loss currently deductible and any limited partnership loss to be carried forward.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident limited partner may deduct allocated losses only to the extent of the at-risk capital actually contributed and not otherwise protected; excess losses are carried forward and cannot be distributed to the partner as cash.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Federal T5013 late filing penalty: C$25 per day per partner, minimum C$100, maximum C$2,500; if the failure is made knowingly or under circumstances of gross negligence, C$100 per day per partner, minimum C$200, maximum C$12,000. Additional gross-negligence penalties may apply where false statements are made in a return.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Revenu Québec — Relevé 15 and Summary of Relevé 15 (partner income information return for a société en commandite / limited partnership); filed through Revenu Québec's Accès Dossier Affaires portal or by prescribed electronic transmission.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; the Relevé 15 is issued to each Quebec-resident or Quebec-taxable partner and the summary is filed with Revenu Québec.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Relevé 15 slips generally must be furnished to partners by the last day of February (or an extended date where filed electronically) and the summary transmitted to Revenu Québec by the applicable March electronic deadline; the underlying partnership information return aligns with the federal five-month deadline following the fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full legal name, address, Quebec enterprise number (NEQ), Social Insurance Number, or Business Number of the limited partner.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident partner without a Canadian identification number, enter the partner's foreign tax identification number, country of residence, and treaty status; no Quebec NEQ is required unless the partner has a Quebec establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total net income from the partnership allocated to the partner and taxable in Quebec.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only income attributable to Canadian sources or a Quebec permanent establishment; exclude foreign-source income of the LP that has no nexus with Canada unless specifically allocated as Quebec-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocated allowable loss, subject to the limited partner's at-risk limitation and Quebec loss-restriction rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident limited partner may apply this loss only against Canadian or Quebec-source income; any excess is governed by federal and Quebec carryforward rules and cannot be converted into a cash distribution.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Percentage of each income or loss class attributable to operations carried on in Quebec for corporate or commercial purposes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the non-resident partner has no permanent establishment in Quebec, leave the percentage nil; if the LP itself has a Quebec permanent establishment, reflect the Quebec-source portion of each partner's allocation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Quebec imposes parallel administrative penalties for late, incomplete, or missing Relevé 15 filings; fines generally range from C$50 to C$2,500 per Relevé, with higher penalties where false statements are made knowingly. Failure to file the partnership information return may also result in the loss of deduction or loss-carryforward privileges at the partner level.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act (Canada) on dividends, deemed dividends, and certain distributions of Canadian portfolio income paid to non-resident persons. If the LP receives dividends from a Canadian corporation and distributes those amounts to a non-resident limited partner, the LP or general partner must withhold 25% unless treaty relief applies. Under the Canada–US Tax Convention, the reduced rate is 15% generally, and 5% where the beneficial owner is a US company owning 10% or more of the voting shares of the Canadian payor.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke treaty relief, the non-resident limited partner must provide to the LP/general partner a completed CRA Form NR301 (Declaration of Eligibility for Benefits Under a Tax Treaty) or NR302 for fee-type payments, accompanied by a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the partner's tax authority. The LP must retain the TRC and supporting computations for six years. If treaty relief is claimed for business profits, the non-resident partner must also file a Canadian income tax return to perfect the exemption. If no TRC is provided, the LP must withhold at the statutory 25%; the non-resident partner can later file a Canadian return to recover the excess withholding.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Canada's statutory Part XIII withholding rate is 25% for both cross-border royalties and interest payments to non-residents. Interest paid to an arm's-length non-resident may be exempt from Part XIII under the Canadian interest-exemption rules and, under most Canadian tax treaties, interest is typically exempt or taxed at a 0% rate. Royalties for patents, trademarks, know-how, and similar intangibles are generally subject to 25% statutory withholding, with treaty-reduced rates, commonly 10% under the Canada–US Convention; certain copyright and computer-software royalties may be exempt. Quebec imposes no separate non-resident withholding on cross-border interest or royalties beyond the federal Part XIII mechanism.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.notes_on_lp_distribution_mechanics: A limited partnership distribution is not automatically a 'dividend' for Canadian withholding purposes. Partners are taxed on allocated income, and actual cash distributions are generally tax-free to the extent of the partner's paid-up capital and previously taxed income. Withholding is triggered only when the distribution consists of Canadian-source payments, such as Canadian dividends, interest, rental income, royalties, or management fees, or when a non-resident partner's allocation is subject to Part I tax payable through a partnership remittance.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CRA Form T106 (Information Return for Non-Arm's Length Transactions With Non-Residents) must be filed by a partnership when the aggregate fair market value of specified transactions with non-arm's length non-resident persons exceeds C$1,000,000 in a fiscal period. Canada does not prescribe separate Monetary Local File or Master File thresholds; however, the CRA expects OECD-aligned contemporaneous documentation for all material cross-border transactions. Penalty protection requires complete, accurate, and contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation even below the T106 threshold where an adjustment is assessed.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not maintain separate Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) of the type applied in zero-tax offshore jurisdictions. However, the federal General Anti-Avoidance Rule (s. 245 of the Income Tax Act) and the parallel Quebec GAAR (s. 1079.2 of the Taxation Act) permit the CRA and Revenu Québec to disregard transactions or arrangements that lack real economic substance and whose sole purpose is to obtain a tax benefit. In addition, the 'sham' doctrine applies where parties present a transaction that is in fact different from its documented form. A SPAC limited partnership must demonstrate genuine commercial objectives, maintain substantive governance and records in Canada, hold its escrowed funds in a real Canadian trust or escrow account, and ensure its sponsor arrangements are arm's-length and commercially rational.
